assumptions.condition: \((X_i,Z_{0i},Z_{1i},(Y_{ik})_{k\geq1})\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed under \(P\) and the specified conditional channel.

novel.justification: Marked repeated-measurement systems, multiscale questionnaires, and panel instruments commonly reveal a growing ordered collection of noisy binary features; a signal bound away from zero is a calibration property of the measurement device.

definitions.name: Resolution-regular complete-mixture RD class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{s,\nu}=\{P:P\text{ is a law on }(X,Z_0,Z_1)\text{ satisfying }\mathrm{ass{:}aggregate\text{-}iid},\mathrm{ass{:}sharp\text{-}cutoff},\mathrm{ass{:}marked\text{-}channel},\mathrm{ass{:}running\text{-}density},\mathrm{ass{:}cutoff\text{-}smoothness},\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}continuity},\mathrm{ass{:}treated\text{-}continuity},\mathrm{ass{:}upper\text{-}resolution\text{-}tail},\mathrm{ass{:}lower\text{-}resolution\text{-}tail},\mathrm{ass{:}decoder\text{-}entropy}\text{ for every }n,m\geq1\}\).

definitions.name: Generic complete-mixture minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(R_{n,m}^{\mathrm{mix}}=\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{s,\nu}}\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\psi-\psi_P\|_{\ell^\infty(\mathcal I_q)}\), where the infimum is over deterministic maps measurable with respect to \(\sigma(O_1^{(m)},\ldots,O_n^{(m)})\), or Markov kernels obtained by adjoining a declared auxiliary random seed independent of the data.

definitions.name: Generic minimax honest-band width
definitions.construction: \(H_{n,m,\alpha}^{\mathrm{mix}}=\inf_{\mathcal C_{n,m}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{s,\nu}}\mathbb E_P\sup_{q\in\mathcal I_q}\{U_{n,m}(q)-L_{n,m}(q)\}\), where the infimum is over data-measurable bands and declared randomized kernels satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{s,\nu}}\Pr_P\{L_{n,m}(q)\leq\psi_P(q)\leq U_{n,m}(q)\ \forall q\in\mathcal I_q\}\geq1-\alpha\).

definitions.name: Decoded local-polynomial estimator
definitions.construction: Compute \(S_{i,m}(q)=\sum_{k=1}^mA_k(q)(2Y_{ik}-1)/\lambda_k\), regress this curve on \(X_i\) separately on the two cutoff sides with local-polynomial order \(\lfloor s\rfloor\) and bandwidth \(h\asymp n^{-1/(2s+1)}\), and define \(\widehat\psi_{n,m}\) as the right boundary fit minus the left boundary fit.

definitions.name: Specified randomized bias-aware band
definitions.construction: Given the data, draw \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\) independently, use their conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile for the supremum of the centered local-polynomial influence process of \(S_{i,m}\), and add the deterministic radii \(L_xh^s\) and \(2L_Am^{-\nu}\) to both endpoints. The resulting Markov kernel is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(O_1^{(m)},\ldots,O_n^{(m)})\vee\sigma(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n)\), and its randomization law is fixed and known.

definitions.name: Canonical unresolved-tail alternatives
definitions.construction: For each \(m\), fix two treated latent states \(z_m^+,z_m^-\in\{-1,1\}^{\mathbb N}\) with \(z_{m,k}^+=z_{m,k}^-=1\) for \(k\leq m\), \(z_{m,k}^+=1\) and \(z_{m,k}^-=-1\) for \(k>m\). Keep the running-variable law and control latent law common, and set the treated mixing laws in a neighborhood of the cutoff to point masses at \(z_m^+\) or \(z_m^-\).

definitions.name: Sparse distribution-valued RD worked specialization
definitions.construction: Let \(Z_d=F_d\) be a random distribution on \([0,1]\), let each resolution coordinate be conditionally independent with law \(F_D\), and take \(\phi(F,q)=Q_F(q)\). For \(m\geq4\), set \(\ell=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\), use the fixed raw-draw halves \(A_m=\{1,\ldots,\ell\}\) and \(B_m=\{\ell+1,\ldots,2\ell\}\), average their two order-statistic interpolants, and combine that average with the full-sample interpolant using coefficients \((m+2)/(m-\ell)\) and \(-(\ell+2)/(m-\ell)\) to form \(J_{i,m}\).

statements.statement: If \(Z_D\) is directly observed, the sharp-cutoff discontinuity satisfies \[\lim_{x\downarrow0}\mathbb E_P[\phi_A(Z,q)\mid X=x]-\lim_{x\uparrow0}\mathbb E_P[\phi_A(Z,q)\mid X=x]=\psi_P(q)\] uniformly in \(q\in\mathcal I_q\). A finite resolution-\(m\) tuple instead identifies \(\Theta_m(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{(m)})\), and no point-identification claim is made for its elements.
statements.justification: The statement cleanly separates the causal continuity argument from the information supplied by a finite tuple.
statements.gap: Van Dijcke (2025, Q1, pp. 25--26) states the corresponding direct-distribution continuity condition; the proposition uses that standard logic without claiming an extension.
statements.consumer: Applied users can distinguish a causal target defined under direct latent observation from the sensitivity set supported by a sparse tuple.

statements.statement:
For every \(m\geq1\), the two laws generated by \(\mathrm{def{:}canonical	ext{-}tail	ext{-}pair}\) belong to \(\mathcal M_{s,
u}\), have identical resolution-\(m\) observed laws, and satisfy \(\|\psi_{P_m^+}-\psi_{P_m^-}\|_\infty\geq2c_Am^{-
u}\). Thus \(\operatorname{diam}_\infty\Theta_m(P_{m,\mathrm{obs}}^{(m)})\geq2c_Am^{-
u}\) for every finite \(m\).
statements.justification: The explicit pair certifies the nonvanishing finite-resolution obstruction without inserting an existential least-favorable assumption into the class.
statements.gap: Generic mixture nonidentification results do not give this exact smoothness-indexed separation inside a nested RD experiment.
statements.consumer: The pair supplies the resolution component of both the minimax-risk and honest-width lower bounds.

statements.statement:
There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class radii, such that for every \(n,m\geq1\), \[c\{n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-
u}\}\leq R_{n,m}^{\mathrm{mix}}\leq C\{n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-
u}\}.\] The deterministic data-measurable estimator \(\widehat\psi_{n,m}\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}decoded	ext{-}rd	ext{-}estimator}\) attains the upper bound. Consequently, bounded \(m\) gives a positive floor, \(1\ll m\ll n^{a_s/
u}\) gives the intermediate frontier \(m^{-
u}\), and \(m\gtrsim m_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)=n^{a_s/
u}\) recovers the oracle rate \(n^{-a_s}\).
statements.justification: This is an explicit two-resolution minimax theorem with bounded, intermediate, and oracle regimes rather than a threshold defined through an unknown modulus.
statements.gap: The complete-mixture literature and the RD literature do not provide a matching frontier for a nested latent functional with a polynomial unresolved tail localized at a boundary.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives a sample-allocation rule for marked latent-feature studies and a benchmark against which sparse distribution-valued designs can be calibrated.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), constants \(0<c_\alpha<C_\alpha<\infty\) satisfy \[c_\alpha\{n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-\nu}\}\leq H_{n,m,\alpha}^{\mathrm{mix}}\leq C_\alpha\{n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-\nu}\}\] for every \(n,m\geq1\). The band in \(\mathrm{def{:}randomized\text{-}band}\), using the declared independent Gaussian multipliers and explicit cutoff and resolution bias radii, is uniformly honest and attains the upper bound, including when the covariance degenerates because the deterministic bias radii remain active.
statements.justification: The theorem makes resolution uncertainty first-order in simultaneous inference and specifies the only external randomization used by the procedure.
statements.gap: Existing honest RD intervals are scalar and single-resolution, while sparse functional-data bands concern additive point-identified observation models.
statements.consumer: The band gives honest uncertainty for an entire indexed latent-functional contrast when within-unit resolution is a binding information constraint.

statements.statement: In the direct distribution-observation experiment, continuity at the cutoff of both potential average-quantile curves implies \[\lim_{x\downarrow0}\mathbb E_P[Q_{F_D}(q)\mid X=x]-\lim_{x\uparrow0}\mathbb E_P[Q_{F_D}(q)\mid X=x]=\tau_P^Q(q)\] for every \(q\in\mathcal I_q\). With only \(m\) conditionally independent draws from \(F_D\), the observed law identifies an operator fiber and need not point identify \(\tau_P^Q\).
statements.justification: The worked specialization preserves the standard causal interpretation while refusing to equate it with finite-tuple point identification.
statements.gap: Van Dijcke (2025, Q1, pp. 25--26) supplies the direct-observation continuity premise; finite-tuple operator fibers are a separate information issue.
statements.consumer: The distinction governs interpretation of the CPS state-income curves produced by \(\mathrm{R3D::r3d}\).

statements.statement: Under bounded-away-from-zero \(C^\beta\) latent densities and one-sided \(C^s\) average-quantile regressions, the fixed-split statistic in \(\mathrm{def{:}r3d\text{-}worked\text{-}specialization}\) is measurable from the raw \(m\) draws and its two halves are averaged before jackknifing. With bandwidth \(h\asymp n^{-1/(2s+1)}\), the resulting estimator satisfies \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\tau_{n,m}^{J}-\tau_P^Q\|_\infty\leq C\{n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-r_\beta}\}\), where \(r_\beta=\min\{(\beta+1)/2,2\}\).
statements.justification: The benchmark records a fully measurable finite-resolution procedure and a conservative rate without asserting that it is the complete-mixture optimum.
statements.gap: Jochmans and Weidner (2024, Section 3.1, pp. 11--12) motivate split-panel bias removal, but not a distribution-valued RD curve with this fixed averaged split.
statements.consumer: The result supplies an implementable resolution correction for \(\mathrm{R3D::r3d}\) while the sharp iid-tuple operator exponent is unresolved.

statements.statement: For the iid distribution-valued tuple operator in \(\mathrm{def{:}r3d\text{-}worked\text{-}specialization}\), what is the sharp operator-specific exponent \(\nu_{\mathrm{R3D}}(\beta,\gamma)\) for the local average-quantile functional, and does its risk equal \(n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-\nu_{\mathrm{R3D}}(\beta,\gamma)}\) uniformly over all joint \((n,m)\) regimes? The Handle is to construct a stable Bernstein--Legendre decoder for the direct bound and a dual moment-annihilating pair of compatible random CDF paths for the converse, with both bounds evaluated in the complete \(m\)-tuple experiment.
statements.justification: This question isolates the genuine unresolved step needed to turn the generic frontier into a sharp R3D specialization.
statements.gap: Peng et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1, p. 9) give fixed-resolution nonidentification, but no matching growing-resolution modulus for compatible smooth latent CDF paths at an RD boundary.
statements.consumer: Its answer determines the smallest CPS cell size at which \(\mathrm{R3D::r3d}\) achieves direct-distribution accuracy.

statements.statement: Can the complete-tuple decoder obtained in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}r3d\text{-}operator\text{-}index}\) be coupled with the declared Gaussian multiplier randomization to produce a cross-quantile-compatible, bias-aware band for \(\tau_P^Q\) whose honest width matches the resulting explicit R3D frontier without a covariance lower bound? The Handle is multiplier studentization of the aggregate influence process plus separate certified cutoff and operator-approximation radii and an unstudentized concentration fallback on low-variance coordinates.
statements.justification: A sharp estimator does not automatically yield an honest simultaneous band when operator bias and boundary bias collide.
statements.gap: Cai and Hu (2025, Theorems 1--3, pp. 7--10, and the band on p. 17) treat additive functional observations, while Peng et al. (2026, Corollary 6.4 and p. 24) use a structural mixing model and a variance condition.
statements.consumer: The resulting band would provide resolution-aware simultaneous uncertainty for the CPS state-income application.

sampling_model.design: Sharp cutoff assignment \(D_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\geq0\}\) with a running density bounded above and below near zero.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) aggregate records are independent draws from one fixed latent law. Resolution \(m\) reveals the first \(m\) coordinates of a nested marked tuple generated conditionally on the observed-arm latent state.
sampling_model.treatment: Direct latent-state observation plus continuity of both potential functional regressions identifies the causal cutoff contrast. A finite tuple identifies only the operator-fiber set \(\Theta_m\).
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment is deterministic at the cutoff; identification uses positive running density and separate continuity of both potential regressions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The generic estimator decodes resolved latent coordinates and applies one-sided local-polynomial smoothing. It is deterministic and data-measurable; the feasible band alone uses declared independent Gaussian multipliers.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Condition Q1 on pp. 25--26 gives cutoff continuity for the direct distribution-valued target, while Proposition 2 and Corollary 3 on p. 30 give the paper's asymptotic process and band conclusions.
Proposition 3.1 on p. 9 gives bounded-sample barycenter nonidentification, while Corollary 6.4 and the display on p. 24 give structural-model simultaneous inference.
Theorem 2 on pp. 8--9 gives sparse, intermediate, and dense sup-norm behavior for an additive functional-data mean model.
Theorems 1--3 on pp. 7--10 and the display on p. 17 give Gaussian approximations and simultaneous bands for an additive functional-data mean model.
Theorem 3.1 on p. 14 and Corollary 3.1 on p. 15 characterize optimal scalar confidence intervals through ordered moduli.
Section 3.1 on pp. 11--12 constructs a split-panel jackknife for leading noisy-proxy distribution and quantile bias.

tldr:
The flagship result is a standalone complete-mixture regression-discontinuity frontier. A latent indexed functional has polynomially decaying unresolved coordinates, each resolution reveals a nested marked tuple, and the causal contrast is localized at a sharp cutoff. Matching minimax risk and all-honest band width equal \(n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-
u}\): bounded resolution leaves a positive floor, intermediate resolution is governed by \(m^{-
u}\), and \(m\asymp n^{s/[
u(2s+1)]}\) is the smallest oracle order. The estimator is data-measurable, the band uses explicitly declared independent Gaussian multipliers, and a smooth unresolved-tail pair supplies the converse. Distribution-valued R3D is a worked specialization: direct latent distributions identify the LAQTE under two potential-curve continuity conditions, finite iid tuples remain partially identifying, and their sharp operator exponent is exposed as an open question rather than attributed to prior R3D theory.

project_justification.gap: Complete-mixture papers study nonidentification or global mixing-law loss, functional-data papers study additive point-identified measurements, and RD papers localize directly observed scalar or distributional functionals. None gives a generic matching two-resolution frontier with a finite-resolution identification floor and an RD boundary term.
project_justification.niche: Nested marked mixture operators with a smooth latent-functional tail isolate the interaction between operator resolution and boundary localization while remaining explicit enough for exact minimax and honest-width statements.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the frontier \(n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-\nu}\), constructs a decoded local-polynomial estimator and a randomized bias-aware band, certifies the lower bound with explicit indistinguishable tail alternatives, and uses sparse distribution-valued R3D as the worked operator-specialization problem.

related_work: Van Dijcke (2025) is informed-by context only: Q1 on pp. 25--26 states the continuity condition for the direct distribution-valued RD target, and Proposition 2 plus Corollary 3 on p. 30 give its asymptotic process and band conclusions. No theorem-level comparison with a Van Dijcke resolution condition is made. Peng, Stijven, Wang, and Gilbert (2026, Proposition 3.1, p. 9) show bounded-sample barycenter nonidentification; Corollary 6.4 and the displayed band on p. 24 concern their structural marginal model. Their operator-fiber distinction informs the R3D open question. Berger, Hermann, and Holzmann (2025, Theorem 2, pp. 8--9) organize additive functional-data estimation into sparse, intermediate, and dense regimes; that organization informs the presentation, while the observation operator and target differ. Cai and Hu (2025, Theorems 1--3, pp. 7--10, and the band on p. 17) provide additive-model simultaneous inference and inform the Gaussian-process component. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, Theorem 3.1, p. 14, and Corollary 3.1, p. 15) inform the bias-aware honesty argument for a scalar regression functional. Jochmans and Weidner (2024, Section 3.1, pp. 11--12) inform the fixed-split averaged-halves R3D benchmark. Calonico, Cattaneo, and Titiunik (2014, Section 2, pp. 2299--2304), Chiang, Hsu, and Sasaki (2019, Theorem 2, p. 16, and Corollary 1, p. 19), and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Theorem 2.1, pp. 1569--1571) supply standard boundary smoothing and uniform approximation tools. Every named paper is methodological context rather than a direct theorem target.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicit generic frontier relies on marked coordinates with uniformly stable decoders and a two-sided polynomial loading tail. Iid draws from a latent distribution do not automatically satisfy that decoder condition. For the R3D specialization, the fixed averaged-halves jackknife gives the upper benchmark \(n^{-s/(2s+1)}+m^{-r_\beta}\), but matching it requires a separate complete-tuple approximation theorem and dual lower construction.
honest_scope: The generic marked-mixture risk and honest-width frontiers, the canonical indistinguishable-tail pair, the direct causal interpretation, and the R3D jackknife benchmark are theorem statements to establish. The R3D-specific complete-tuple exponent and a matching bias-aware studentized LAQTE band remain open. Direct latent-distribution observation and finite-tuple observation are distinct experiments throughout.

literature_map.settled: Q1 of Van Dijcke (2025, pp. 25--26) states direct-target continuity, and Proposition 2 plus Corollary 3 (p. 30) give its process and band results; Chiang, Hsu, and Sasaki give uniform scalar quantile-RD inference.
literature_map.open_boundary: Finite iid distribution tuples identify an operator fiber whose sharp average-quantile resolution exponent is unknown.

literature_map.settled: Bounded grouped samples can fail to identify barycenter quantiles, and split-panel jackknifing can remove leading noisy-proxy bias.
literature_map.open_boundary: Neither result supplies a matching growing-resolution complete-tuple modulus at an RD boundary.

literature_map.settled: Additive functional-data models have sparse-to-dense estimation and Gaussian-approximation regimes.
literature_map.open_boundary: Those models are point identified at fixed resolution and do not have a complete-mixture identification floor.

literature_map.settled: Ordered moduli, robust boundary bias control, and Gaussian approximation provide the component tools for honest inference.
literature_map.open_boundary: The complete-mixture width must add a resolution-identification radius to boundary and stochastic terms.
